conventions.plan: x along the host sheet's helices, y across them, origin at the tile centre
conventions.z: positive upward, away from the electrode; §1's bias pulls the tile down
conventions.duplex in plan: a rectangle of width d = 2.69 nm (SAXS), so two parallel duplexes at exactly d are TANGENT and admissible — `C-0041`'s convention verbatim
conventions.hinge arm: one rectangle arm x d, ROOTED at its hinge rather than centred on it, owning NO vertical member: its near end is a crossover in the host's own plane and its far end is `C-0034`'s two-link A2 joint
conventions.hinge site: a crossover of the host's own lattice; interface b carries the columns of parity b mod 2, so an interior row sees both parities at a 16 bp pitch and an edge row one parity at 32 bp
conventions.buried crossover: a crossover lying under an arm on one of that arm's own two interfaces; it would tie a free lever back to the sheet, so it is charged as deleted
conventions.orientation sweep: over [0, 2pi) for a rooted arm and [0, pi) for `C-0041`'s centred beam

predicates.P6 the flatness consequence of the colum: the LATTICE placement carries 3 arms per interior row and 2 per edge row, i.e. 3 attachment columns, exactly `C-0047`'s break-even; on `C-0015`'s inherited half-offset grid the same arm admits only 2 columns, because a ROOTED arm in the outermost column overhangs the edge. At three columns `C-0047` reports 0.218 of the stroke (CITED, for a regular 3 x 15), against its 0.10 tolerance and against 0.308 for no coupling at all — so the array is NOT a net dishing source, which `C-0041`'s 1 x 15 is at 2.26x. FALSIFIER 5 FIRED — three columns are admitted and the flatness break-even is met
predicates.P7 which variable must give, as a thresh: TWO variables, and the second is the binding one. (i) The crossover LATTICE: 45 arms need 45 distinct crossovers and the lattice places 43, so the host edge would have to reach 49.25 nm (1.23x) or the duplex count 16 (1.07x). (ii) The host's own SURVIVAL: it stays in one piece only up to 25 arms, 1.80x below the 45 demanded and 1.72x below the 43 the lattice would place — so the threshold is not 45 -> 43, it is 45 -> 25. The arm itself is a PLACED quantity and cannot simply be shortened; shortening it needs a smaller path count, which is the same variable.

findings.the verdict: `C-0041`'s answer does NOT transfer, and neither of its two obstructions survives contact with `E5a1`. As BODIES the array packs: 1105 nm2 is 0.685 of the footprint, the arm owns no standoff and no tie so the level-independent clash cannot arise at any tilt, and arm + d = 11.82 nm sits UNDER the 13.33 nm column pitch where `C-0041`'s span sat 2.59x over it. What refuses the array is the HINGE LATTICE: an arm must root on a crossover, a row's roots sit at a 5.44 nm pitch (10.88 on the two edge rows) and an arm needs 11.82 nm of clearance, so a row carries two or three and the tile carries 43 of the 45 demanded, at the best of all 32 phases.
findings.the binding currency is a lattice pitch,: `C-0040` counted the INVENTORY and found 49-56 against 45 demanded — 80-92 %, tight but not refused. Placement is a different question and it is refused: the crossovers a row can actually reach are those of its own two interfaces, and consecutive ones are 5.44 nm apart against an arm that needs 11.82. A row therefore SKIPS two sites out of every three. An inventory is a sum over the sheet; a placement is a constraint per row, and the two differ by 2 arms.
findings.the edge rows are the ones that lose: An interior row is bounded by two interfaces of OPPOSITE parity, so it sees every column of the 16 bp lattice; an edge row sees one interface and therefore one parity, at twice the pitch. That asymmetry is not imposed anywhere — it falls out of `C-0015`'s alternation — and it is worth an arm on each of the two edge rows.
findings.what the host pays even for the arms it: 65.4 % of the host's own duplex length stops being sheet and becomes lever, and 56 crossovers of 56 are spent or buried (1.00x of the inventory). The residual host is SEVERED, in 0 components with 0 crossovers left of 56. WHICH BODY HOSTS THE HINGES IS THEREFORE A DESIGN VARIABLE and nothing upstream has chosen it: `C-0039` grounds the near end on the TILE, and the tile is the body whose own rigidity `C-0006`, `C-0009` and `C-0047` spend on flatness.
findings.a rooted arm has a direction and a centr: `C-0041` swept [0, pi) because its beam is centred on its tie and therefore symmetric under a half turn. A hinge arm is rooted, so theta and theta + pi are DIFFERENT DESIGNS and the sweep must run over the full circle. It is worth a factor of two in the sweep and, more usefully, a factor of two in what a cluster of hinge sites can carry — one arm each way from a cluster narrower than a single arm.
findings.the count is a fixed point and it is 43,: The arm is a PLACED quantity, so fewer paths ask for a shorter arm and a shorter arm places more easily; the count the lattice carries is therefore a fixed point, and it is 43 at a 8.966 nm arm. That is not the escape the two missing arms make it look like: at 43 paths the host spends 49 of its 49 crossovers, keeps 0, and has NO bonded component at all. The count that leaves the host whole is 25, at a 7.236 nm arm — 1.80x below §3's 45 — and the connected part collapses steeply above it: 15 duplexes bonded at 25 arms, 14 at 30, 8 at 35, 3 at 40 and none at 42.
findings.the per-path force is untouched by any o: 2.22 pN per path at §3's acceptable stroke against the 10 pN unzip allowable — 4.50x of margin — so nothing here is an allowable failure. The array is refused by the lattice, not by a force.
